purpose: Targeted additions to data/train aimed at the failure families measured on baseline-needle3-c9d915eca282. One example family per observed defect, not a general enlargement of the corpus.
_rule: Every entry below names a family that ACTUALLY OCCURS in the baseline cases.jsonl. No example targets a defect nobody measured, and no example reuses an eval utterance — `python -m vesta_router validate` checks disjointness by id and by normalized utterance, and passed after this change.

addedByFamily._note: Counts overlap and do not sum to 39: one no-tool trap answers both false-positive families, and a missing-slot example that stops a scraped value answers the execution family and the lexical-grounded one. The per-example list below is the authoritative mapping and these totals are derived from it.

examples.because: neg.capital — a general-knowledge question containing a proper noun came back as search_contacts {query: "Australia"}, and that call is grounded, so the guard admits it.
the same shape in Italian; baseline tool selection over the five Italian cases was 0.5.
neg.typo.thanks — an acknowledgement produced get_time {}, which has no required arguments and therefore always survives the guard.
a tool's name as the SUBJECT of a question rather than as a request; the baseline treats the noun as the trigger.
neg.time-philosophy — "Time really flies when you're busy." produced get_time {}.
neg.cat-name — a weekday used as a subject became create_event {title, start: "Monday"}; every token of it is in the sentence, so it is grounded and wrong.
neg.navigate-story — a place name inside past-tense narration produced get_time {place: "Piazza Garibaldi"}.
neg.calendar-observation — a remark about a full week produced get_calendar_events {}.
neg.tasker-memory — "I used Tasker years ago." produced search_contacts {query: "Tasker"}.
an Italian calendar remark; the no-tool corpus carries only one Italian near-miss.
neg.woke-at-730 — "I woke up at 7:30." became set_alarm {time: "7:30"}; the digit clock time is the trap and the existing trap example uses a worded one.
neg.sms-complaint — an inbound message described in the third person produced send_sms with an invented contact AND an invented body.
the negation cases in the corpus cover alarm, call, timer and SMS; navigation had none, and navigate_to is where the baseline scraped a destination out of the verb.
neg.hypothetical — a question about a zero-minute timer produced set_timer {minutes: 0}.
negation in Italian on the highest-cost tool; the corpus had negation in Italian only for an alarm.
slot.sms.no-text — "Send Marco a text." came back as text: "a text". The words are in the sentence, so grounding admits it and a message saying "a text" would be sent.
slot.navigate.bare — "Start navigation." came back as destination: "navigation".
slot.reminder.no-text — "Remind me at 4pm." came back as text: "Remind me".
slot.alarm.bare.it — "Mettimi una sveglia." came back as time: "now".
slot.event.no-start — a titled appointment with no time came back as start: "now".
slot.call.bare — "Make a call." came back as contact: "".
pos.timer.seconds — "90 seconds" came back as minutes: 90, the number copied rather than converted.
pos.timer.seconds.half — "30 seconds" came back as minutes: 30.
pos.timer.compound — "1 minute 30 seconds" came back as minutes: 130, the two units concatenated.
pos.timer.minutes.it — the only case in the corpus where a clear request produced no call at all was an Italian timer.
a 12-hour time has to reach the tool as 24-hour HH:MM; the corpus taught worded times but no pm-suffixed one.
pos.alarm.time and pos.alarm.stt both produced "7:30" where the schema's format is HH:MM and the corpus asks for "07:30".
pos.alarm.time also emitted date: "tomorrow", an unexpected extra argument. set_alarm.date is declared YYYY-MM-DD, "tomorrow" is not one, and Vesta resolves relative days at dispatch.
pos.reminder.both and slot.followup.keeps-known both passed the user's "3pm"/"4pm" through unconverted.
pos.event.title-start — "Friday at noon" was passed through verbatim rather than as "Friday 12:00".
pos.time.elsewhere — get_time was called with the place but without kind: "time".
pos.document.query — the query dropped the subject of the question and kept only the document name.

stale.calendar.no-invented-date — a bare calendar question after a dated one carried the previous date forward. get_calendar_events has no required argument, so nothing refuses it and the answer is silently about the wrong day. The existing example's utterance names a day; this one names none.
navigation had no stale-context example, and a pronoun reference to a prior destination is the same shape as stale.call.other-contact.
stale.reminder.other-text — a new reminder with a time reused the PREVIOUS reminder's text.

stale.cancellation.explicit — "cancel that, forget the timer" emitted the pending timer anyway. The existing cancellation examples do not name the tool in the cancelling sentence, and naming it is what the baseline latched onto.
stale.cancellation.it — "lascia stare" produced set_alarm {time: "07:00"}, an invented time on an abandoned action.
the unit conversions were taught only on whole requests, never on a bare slot-fill answer, which is where the app actually asks.
slot.followup.time — a worded time filled into a pending alarm came back as "7:30" and with a spurious label: "Missing=time".
